title: Universal homeomorphisms induce equivalences of small pro-etale topoi
statement:
Let $r:X\to Y$ be a universal homeomorphism of schemes [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Use the small pro-etale sites with compatible size conventions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and the induced inverse and direct image adjunction $r^{-1}\dashv r_*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then these functors are quasi-inverse equivalences
$$
 r^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}}):r_*.
$$
In particular its unit $F\to r_*r^{-1}F$ and counit $r^{-1}r_*G\to G$ are isomorphisms for every sheaf of sets $F$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $G$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$.

source.place: Tag 09AB (proetale-lemma-thickening), with Tag 04DF (morphisms-lemma-universal-homeomorphism) identifying universal homeomorphisms with integral universally injective surjective morphisms.

proof.text: First construct a cover by pairs of affine opens. Choose affine opens $X_a$ covering $X$. Since $r$ is a homeomorphism, $Y_a=r(X_a)$ is open, and $r^{-1}(Y_a)=X_a$. The restriction $r_a:X_a\to Y_a$ is a universal homeomorphism: each of its base changes is a base change of $r$. In particular it is surjective and universally closed. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-affine-target] to conclude that $Y_a$ is affine. Thus $(X_a,Y_a)$ are matching affine covers, without assuming that $r$ is finite or that either scheme is quasi-separated. The argument below first treats an arbitrary universal homeomorphism between affine schemes, and then applies it to each $r_a$.

source.place: Tag 09AB, first reduction; limits.tex Tag 05YU (proposition-affine) supplies the matching affine cover

proof.text: Suppose now $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Base change along $r$ is an equivalence of the categories of etale schemes by [lemma-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-site-equivalence]. It restricts to affine etale schemes: base change of an affine scheme over an affine base is the spectrum of the tensor product, by the ring-map and fibre-product universal properties [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. Conversely, if an etale $V\to Y$ has affine pullback $V_X$, the map $V_X\to V$ is a universal homeomorphism and hence surjective and universally closed, so [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-affine-target] makes $V$ affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization], the coordinate algebras of all these affine etale objects are finitely presented. Taking opposites therefore gives an equivalence $E:C\mapsto B\otimes_A C$ between etale $A$-algebras and etale $B$-algebras, with a functorial quasi-inverse on those categories.

For later use, if $P$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra and $(D_j)$ a small filtered diagram of commutative $R$-algebras, then $\varinjlim_j\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,D_j)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,\varinjlim_jD_j)$ is bijective. Surjectivity is exactly [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit], after [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] identifies the algebra colimit with the ring colimit. For injectivity choose finitely many generators of $P$, put two representative maps at a common index, and apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] with $N=R$ to their differences on these generators, using $D_j\otimes_RR=D_j$. Filteredness puts the finitely many resulting equalities at one later index, where the two homomorphisms are equal on every generator and hence equal. This also handles zero generators; filtered categories are nonempty [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 00QO (lemma-characterize-finite-presentation), finite-generator proof, with its filtered-category formulation as in Tag 07C3

proof.text: Extend the equivalence $E$ of step 2 to ind-etale algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Tensor product commutes with these colimits: maps from either $B\otimes_A\varinjlim_i C_i$ or $\varinjlim_i(B\otimes_A C_i)$ to a $B$-algebra are precisely compatible $A$-algebra maps $C_i$ into that algebra, so the canonical comparison is invertible by the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For presentations $C=\varinjlim_i C_i$ and $D=\varinjlim_j D_j$ with etale finitely presented terms, the universal property and step 3 give the natural formula $\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,D)=\varprojlim_i\varinjlim_j\operatorname{Hom}_A(C_i,D_j)$. The same formula over $B$ and the full faithfulness of $E$ on each pair of terms prove full faithfulness on ind-etale algebras. Given an ind-etale $B$-algebra $D=\varinjlim_j D_j$, apply the quasi-inverse of $E$ to the entire diagram, including its arrows, and form $C=\varinjlim_j E^{-1}(D_j)$; these colimits exist by [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist]. Its base change is $D$, proving essential surjectivity. Opposite affine spectra give an equivalence $u:\mathcal B_Y\simeq\mathcal B_X$ of the affine ind-etale categories [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. All diagrams are small in the compatible universes of the item; no fixed bound smaller than the allowed universe is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09AB, passage from etale algebras to ind-etale algebras, expanded by the Hom formula of algebra.tex Tag 00QO

proof.text: Verify the covering assertion omitted by the source. In either affine ind-etale category, a finite family of arrows with target $V$ is a covering exactly when it is jointly surjective. Indeed every arrow is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], and every arrow between affine schemes has affine inverse images of affine opens: on principal opens the inverse images are the corresponding principal spectra, and the affine-morphism criterion [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] extends this to all affine opens. Thus the finitely many inverse images of any affine open of $V$ themselves give the finite affine opens required in the fpqc covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; necessity of surjectivity follows from that same definition. For each $V\in\mathcal B_Y$, the projection $V_X\to V$ and the analogous projections for all domains are homeomorphisms by [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Their commuting squares identify the images of the arrows, so their union is all of $V$ if and only if the base-changed union is all of $V_X$. Consequently $u$ preserves and reflects finite basis coverings, including the empty covering of the empty object. Now let $\{U_i\to V\}_{i\in I}$ be an arbitrary family of arrows of $\mathcal B_Y$, with coverings induced from the pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. It is a covering if and only if some finite subfamily is jointly surjective: if it is a covering, the covering definition applied to the affine open $V$ itself gives finitely many affine opens of some $U_{i_1},\dots,U_{i_n}$ whose images cover $V$; conversely, if a finite subfamily is jointly surjective, all arrows are weakly etale and, for every affine open $W\subset V$, the affine inverse images of $W$ in $U_{i_1},\dots,U_{i_n}$ have images covering $W$. The same holds in $\mathcal B_X$, and $u$ preserves and reflects joint surjectivity of finite subfamilies by the homeomorphism argument above. Therefore $\{U_i\to V\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal B_Y$ if and only if $\{u(U_i)\to u(V)\}$ is a covering of $\mathcal B_X$. This is the family-level hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-is-morphism-of-sites] used in step 6. (This also agrees with [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]: every covering of a basis object refines to a finite basis covering.)

source.place: Tag 09AB, omitted verification of coverings; Tag 098E (definition-standard-proetale) and Tag 098X (lemma-affine-alternative)

proof.text: Pass from the bases to sheaves with [lem-cbc-local-dense-ordinary-sheaves], applied to each full inclusion $\mathcal B_T\hookrightarrow T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $T=X,Y$. Its cover-density hypothesis is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. For full inclusions the sieves $L_b$ and $E_{f,g}$ in the comparison statement are maximal: lift $b$ by fullness, and use faithfulness for $f=g$. The induced topology criterion follows because every ambient cover of a basis object refines to a finite basis cover, again by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Sets in the larger universe have all the small comma-category limits required by that theorem. Thus restriction to each basis is an equivalence of categories of set sheaves. The equivalence of bases from steps 4 and 5 induces a sheaf equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-is-morphism-of-sites], clause (3). For $G$ on $X$, the square of these restriction functors commutes: on $V\in\mathcal B_Y$ both composites have value $G(V_X)$ and the same restriction maps [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Therefore the actual direct image $r_*$ is an equivalence when $X,Y$ are affine.

source.place: Tag 098X (lemma-affine-alternative), used at the end of the proof of Tag 09AB; sites.tex Tag 03A0

proof.text: In the affine case the actual adjunction $L=r^{-1}\dashv R=r_*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] has invertible unit and counit. To check this for its specified maps, apply [lem-coef-adjunction-equivalence-counit-iso] to the opposite adjunction $R^{\mathrm{op}}\dashv L^{\mathrm{op}}$: its left adjoint is an equivalence by step 6, so its counit, which is the opposite of $\eta$, is invertible. The triangle $R(\varepsilon_G)\circ\eta_{RG}=1$ then makes $R(\varepsilon_G)$ invertible. Since $R$ is fully faithful, lift its inverse to a morphism $G\to LRG$; faithfulness checks both inverse identities. Thus $\varepsilon_G$ itself is invertible. These are the canonical adjunction maps, rather than unspecified isomorphisms of the two composites.

source.place: Tag 09AB, conclusion about the inverse/direct image adjunction; Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/FullyFaithful.lean:247-249 for the formal adjunction argument

proof.text: Return to the matching affine covers of step 1. For an open immersion $W\hookrightarrow T$, the small pro-etale site of $W$ is the slice of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ over $W$, by clause (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], whose hypotheses explicitly include open immersions and whose conclusion identifies the sites and their set sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-slice-site-localization] to $u_r$ and each $Y_a$. It identifies the restriction of $r_*$ with $(r_a)_*$ and the restriction of $r^{-1}$ with $(r_a)^{-1}$. These comparisons carry the unit and counit to the localized adjunction maps: the direct-image comparison is the identity on $G(V_X)$, the unit on a presheaf section is the coprojection indexed by $(V,\mathrm{id}_{V_X})$, and the counit on a representative $[V,\phi,s]$ is $G(\phi)(s)$, using [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Restriction keeps those formulas, and their sheafifications are uniquely determined by them. Step 7 therefore makes the restricted unit and counit invertible on every $Y_a$ and $X_a$, respectively. The cover-local isomorphism criterion [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] makes them invertible globally: every object has its covering obtained by pullback of these Zariski open covers. Hence $r^{-1}$ and $r_*$ with their given adjunction are quasi-inverse equivalences as claimed.

from.place: Proof, opening site-equivalence paragraph: 'Its inverse functors are r^{-1} and r_*, so the two categories of etale sheaves are equivalent'; the pro-etale counterpart needed by the coefficient conventions.

split_report.summary: Expanded the Stacks affine ind-etale route in eight steps. Reused existing etale invariance, affineness descent, finite-presentation factorization and eventual equality, basis comparison, and localization nodes. Made the source's omitted covering check explicit and checked the actual unit and counit. No new nodes or statement corrections. The source Lean theorem contains sorry and addresses abelian-valued sheaves, so there is no attachment.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the opening site-equivalence paragraph of i-topology: its pro-etale counterpart is proved through affine ind-etale bases, then localized. No assertion that all weakly-etale objects descend as objects is needed; the derived and constructibility clauses belong to i-topology, not this item.

tool_uses.why: Affineness descent supplies matching affine opens and reflection of affine objects in the etale equivalence; this is a generic geometry tool, not a replacement for the unit topological-invariance route.
Finite-presentation compactness supplies the stage factorization in the ind-etale Hom formula; no node of this unit states this algebra tool.
Eventual vanishing with N=R proves equality of maps at a finite stage on finitely many generators.
Constructs the small filtered colimit of the diagram descended by the etale quasi-inverse.
Supplies weak etaleness of all arrows in the affine ind-etale basis.
Supplies the canonical set-sheaf localization comparisons used to return from affine pairs to general schemes.
Only clause (1), identification of the pro-etale site over an open object with the slice site, is used; it explicitly includes open immersions.
Generic adjunction lemma applied to opposite categories identifies the actual unit as an isomorphism.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q87-8edad1c2f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all eight steps in full, the statements of all 24 cited nodes, unit sk-i-topology and parent i-topology, and the sources: Stacks proetale 09AB (lemma-thickening, l.4962-4986), 098X (lemma-affine-alternative) and etale-cohomology 05YX (remark-affine-inside-equivalence, l.6537). I checked in tags/tags that 04DF, 04DZ, 05YU, 03CF and 04TQ name the cited labels. Statement: the universal-homeomorphism hypothesis equals 09AB's 'integral, universally injective, surjective' by 04DF, and the conclusion is the 09AB topos equivalence for sheaves of sets, with the canonical unit and counit. Nothing is added or weakened, and the parent uses it only for sets before its own module lift. Steps: step 1 checks the hypotheses of 05YU on matched affine opens. Step 2 is the etale equivalence restricted to affines, matching 05YX. Step 3: factorization gives surjectivity, and the tensor eventual-zero lemma with N=R gives injectivity. Step 4: full faithfulness from the ind-Hom formula, and essential surjectivity via the quasi-inverse applied to the whole diagram plus small colimits. Step 5: weakly etale arrows plus affine preimages give the fpqc condition, and the homeomorphic projections show joint surjectivity is preserved and reflected. Step 6: I checked every hypothesis of the dense-subsite theorem, including the covering-sieve criterion, which holds by fullness, and that the square of restrictions is G(V_X). Step 7: opposite-adjunction argument, then the triangle identity and full faithfulness. Step 8: slice identification (clause 1), 03CF comparisons, unit and counit compatibility from the section formulas, and gluing over a Zariski cover with isIso_of_coversTop. Edge cases checked: empty scheme, identity, purely inseparable field extension, integral but non-finite maps, non-quasi-separated schemes. Duplicate search: rg for 09AB and for universal homeomorphism with pro-etale; the only related node, a condensed closed-surjective-immersion result, is narrower and not a duplicate. review_split PASS, no undeclared route departures; I accept the eight declared tool_uses as generic tools. No SGA. Repair: step 5 only showed that u identifies the generated topologies, but step 6 cites clause (3) of lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-is-morphism-of-sites, which needs arbitrary, possibly infinite, families to match. I added the argument: a basis family over an affine V is a covering iff some finite subfamily is jointly surjective, and u preserves and reflects this. I also added def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis to step 5 uses; it was already in proof_deps. Corrected file: fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance.json.
